oidc_jwt.description: Access tokens do not automatically include the requesting frontend client as audience.
oidc_jwt.source: Audience support documentation
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag missing frontend client_id in aud as an audience-binding bug unless a mapper/scope was configured to add it.

oidc_jwt.description: Default ACR Values act as defaults and can be overridden by acr_values in the request; they are not a hard enforcement control.
oidc_jwt.source: Advanced configuration / ACR to LoA Mapping
oidc_jwt.note: A lower-than-default acr after an explicit request is by design unless Minimum ACR Value is configured.

oidc_jwt.description: A client scope with role scope mappings is omitted unless the user has an intersecting role.
oidc_jwt.source: Client scopes permissions
oidc_jwt.note: Missing claims or scope entries can be expected due to role-scope filtering, not authorization loss.

oidc_jwt.description: Default ACR Values provide a default requested level but do not reliably enforce that level because the client or user can request a lower acr_values.
oidc_jwt.source: Advanced configuration - ACR to Level of Authentication Mapping
oidc_jwt.note: Do not treat successful lower-ACR authentication as a bypass when only Default ACR Values were configured.

oidc_jwt.description: Restriction of exchanged scopes to the original subject_token scopes is enforced only when the downscope-assertion-grant-enforcer client policy executor is applied.
oidc_jwt.source: Client scopes - Downscoping; Client Policies executors
oidc_jwt.note: Expanded scope on token exchange may reflect missing hardening policy rather than an implementation bug.

oidc_jwt.description: Optional client scopes are only applied when explicitly requested via the scope parameter.
oidc_jwt.source: Client scopes linking
oidc_jwt.note: Claims or audiences from optional scopes being absent is expected unless the scope was requested.

oidc_jwt.description: If PKCE method is left blank, Keycloak allows authorization code flow without requiring PKCE, though PKCE can still be used if sent.
oidc_jwt.source: Basic configuration / PKCE method
oidc_jwt.note: Do not report missing PKCE enforcement as a bug when the client was not configured to require it.

oidc_jwt.description: Client credentials grant returns only an access token by default and does not create a user session or refresh token.
oidc_jwt.source: Using a service account
oidc_jwt.note: Absence of refresh token or session state is expected for service-account logins.

oidc_jwt.description: JWT bearer assertions and access tokens are generally stateless; documentation does not describe jti replay tracking for ordinary JWT auth, and service-account access tokens are bearer tokens revoked via revocation endpoint rather than one-time credentials.
oidc_jwt.source: Using a service account; OpenID Connect token/revocation documentation references
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag replay of the same bearer token or JWT without jti tracking as a vulnerability unless the specific flow promises one-time semantics.

oidc_jwt.description: JWT bearer replay is not documented as being tracked via jti for ordinary stateless JWT validation.
oidc_jwt.source: JWT-related docs and standard behavior
oidc_jwt.note: Reusing the same JWT may be by design unless testing a context with explicit one-time semantics.

oidc_jwt.description: Default ACR values act as defaults and can be overridden by acr_values or claims in the request; they do not reliably enforce a minimum level.
oidc_jwt.source: Advanced configuration / ACR to LoA Mapping
oidc_jwt.note: A lower-than-expected acr may be by design unless Minimum ACR Value is configured.

oidc_jwt.description: Lightweight access tokens intentionally omit many claims and require introspection to recover them.
oidc_jwt.source: Protocol mappers / Using lightweight access token
oidc_jwt.note: Do not treat missing profile/email/groups claims in the access token as a mapping failure when lightweight tokens are enabled.

oidc_jwt.constraint: Valid Redirect URIs use exact case-sensitive string matching by default; only suffix wildcards are supported, and wildcard matching is disabled when the supplied redirect URI contains userinfo or parent-directory path traversal (/../). For I3 redirect_uri_mismatch tests, use explicitly registered redirect URIs and do not assume broad wildcard behavior.

The full wildcard '*' can be configured as a valid redirect URI and matches any http or https redirect URI. This is by design but insecure. For security tests, never rely on '*' unless explicitly testing unspecific redirect URI behavior; otherwise register exact redirect URIs to avoid false positives.

PKCE method has sentinel semantics: blank means PKCE is optional and only enforced if the client sends PKCE parameters; 'S256' or 'plain' require that exact method. For I3/OIDC PKCE tests, configure pkce_code_challenge_method explicitly. Leaving it blank does not disable PKCE support, it disables PKCE requirement.

For OIDC request-object and authorization-request integrity tests, parameters such as claims and acr_values can be changed by the user in the browser URL. Keycloak documentation explicitly recommends PAR or signed request objects to prevent tampering. Do not interpret successful parameter tampering as a broker flaw unless the client was configured to require protected requests.

Default ACR Values do not enforce authentication strength. A user can override them with acr_values in the request. For I5 authorization-binding tests involving ACR/LoA, use Minimum ACR Value or validate the returned acr claim; do not assume default ACR values are an enforcement control.

For I3 config-change sequences, Keycloak applies new client and client-policy configuration to new logins. A valid coherence test must compare behavior of the same flow before and after config change, not treat an admin-initiated policy update itself as a bug.

Audience in access tokens is not automatically the frontend client itself. By design, audience is added through Audience Resolve or Audience protocol mappers/client scopes. For I5 audience tests, configure audience-producing mappers/scopes first; otherwise missing aud is expected and not a vulnerability.

Client scopes permissions are intersection-based: if a client scope has role scope mappings, the user must hold at least one mapped role or the scope and its mappers are omitted from the token. For I5 scope/audience tests, ensure the test user has the required roles; otherwise missing claims are expected due to scope permission filtering.

Downscoping enforcement for token exchange is not default behavior. It requires the client policy executor 'downscope-assertion-grant-enforcer'. For I5 token_exchange_scope_escalation tests, configure this executor when testing hardened behavior; without it, broader requested scopes may reflect normal platform configuration rather than a bug.

Claim enforcement for assertion grants in client policies uses Java regex matching. For I5 claim-binding tests, treat these constraints as regex-based, not exact-only. Escaping matters; wildcard-like patterns are regex semantics, not glob semantics.

Client secret rotation is not automatic. Rotation occurs only on client update, regenerate-secret action, or explicit Admin REST force rotation. For I3 secret/key rotation tests, trigger an update or regenerate action after changing policy; otherwise expecting immediate rotation is incorrect.

Client secret rotation has numeric sentinel semantics: Rotated Secret Expiration value 0 means the old secret is immediately removed during rotation, not 'use default'. Secret Expiration and Remaining Expiration Time are literal seconds. Rotated Secret Expiration must be smaller than Secret Expiration.

Authentication sessions expire after the realm Login timeout, 30 minutes by default. In multi-tab/browser OIDC flows, expired authentication sessions can cause protocol-specific errors and automatic restart. For I3 flow-coherence tests, keep authorization-code sequences within the authentication-session lifetime to avoid false positives from expired auth sessions.

User session count limiter has numeric sentinel semantics: realm max sessions 0 disables the check; client max sessions 0 disables the check. This is a literal disable sentinel, not a default value. If enabled with 'deny new session', repeated login attempts may fail due to session limits rather than the tested invariant.

Service-account client_credentials tokens create no user session and usually no refresh token by default. Logout is unnecessary, though revocation endpoint can revoke issued access tokens. Do not expect user-session inspection semantics from service-account tokens.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests, include a control request using a valid token in the same realm/client configuration. A failed JWT/assertion grant can also result from client policy, missing grant enablement, or client authentication misconfiguration, not just token freshness checks.

Valid Redirect URIs use exact case-sensitive string matching by default. Wildcards are only supported at the end of the pattern, and if the passed redirect URI contains userinfo or parent-directory traversal (/../), wildcard comparison is disabled and exact matching is used. For I3 redirect_uri_mismatch tests, the fuzzer MUST register the exact redirect_uri it will send unless intentionally testing rejection; do not assume broad wildcard matching.

The full wildcard '*' can be configured as a valid redirect URI and allows any http or https redirect URI. This is documented but insecure. For I1/I3/OIDC request-object and redirect tests, the fuzzer MUST NOT use '*' in baseline setups because it makes redirect validation trivially permissive and invalidates mismatch findings.

PKCE method has sentinel semantics: blank means PKCE is not required, but PKCE is still accepted if the client sends PKCE parameters; 'S256' or 'plain' require that method. For pkce_skip and flow-coherence tests, the fuzzer MUST distinguish blank from enforced PKCE and MUST configure S256 or plain when testing mandatory PKCE enforcement.

Default ACR Values do not enforce authentication strength. A user can explicitly send acr_values with a lower level and Keycloak will use that lower level unless Minimum ACR Value is configured. For I5 authorization-binding tests around ACR/LoA, the fuzzer MUST use Minimum ACR Value for enforcement tests and MUST NOT treat Default ACR Values as a server-side restriction.

Step-up LoA Max Age has sentinel semantics: value 0 means the level is valid only for the current authentication and must be re-authenticated on subsequent requests; positive values are seconds of reuse; examples show 36000 for long reuse. Never assume 0 disables the check. For I2/I3 freshness/coherence tests involving ACR/LoA, the fuzzer MUST account for 0 meaning strict re-authentication.

Authentication sessions expire after the realm Login timeout, 30 minutes by default. Multi-tab/browser retries may restart authentication automatically. For I3 state-swap and flow-coherence tests, the fuzzer MUST keep authorization-code flows within the authentication-session lifetime and must not interpret an expired authentication session restart as a state-binding vulnerability.

Client Session Idle, Client Session Max, Access Token Lifespan, Client Offline Session Idle, and Client Offline Session Max are client-level timeout overrides. These are lifetime controls, not per-call budgets. However, verify_granted_identity and verify_read_secret may fail after expiry if the token/session is too short-lived. For I2 tests, the fuzzer SHOULD keep baseline tokens comfortably valid through both verification calls unless intentionally testing expiry.

User session count limiter has sentinel semantics: realm max sessions = 0 disables the check; client max sessions = 0 disables the check. This is not a token-use budget but a concurrent-session limit. For login replay/coherence tests, the fuzzer MUST avoid enabling session-count limiting unless explicitly testing it, because second logins may be denied or may terminate the oldest session by design.

Hashing iterations password policy has sentinel semantics: value -1 means use the algorithm default, not disable hashing iterations. Defaults depend on algorithm (argon2=5, pbkdf2-sha512=210000, pbkdf2-sha256=600000, pbkdf2=1300000). Never assume -1 disables the underlying check.

Maximum Authentication Age password policy has sentinel semantics: value 0 means the user must always re-authenticate with the current password before updating the password. Never assume 0 means unlimited.

WebAuthn timeout has sentinel semantics: value 0 delegates behavior to the authenticator/browser implementation, not literal immediate timeout and not disabled verification. Never assume 0 disables WebAuthn timeout enforcement.

For I1 issuer/request integrity tests using OIDC request objects, Keycloak documentation states client policies can enforce request object security and request object signing algorithm. If request object signature algorithm is not explicitly enforced, tests for unsigned or weakly signed request objects may pass trivially because no validation policy was configured. The fuzzer MUST configure request object signing enforcement before testing oidc_request_object_alg_none.

For I1 alg_none/resign_attacker_key tests on JWT client authentication or JWT-based grants, Keycloak supports multiple client authenticators and JWT assertion modes. The fuzzer MUST configure the client to use Signed JWT authentication and, where applicable, enforce the signature algorithm and trusted key source (certificate/JWKS/IdP). Otherwise failures or successes are not attributable to JWT signature validation.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests against JWT assertions, Keycloak documents Max expiration for Signed JWT client authentication and notes tokens should be issued right before authentication, 60 seconds by default. The fuzzer MUST include a control assertion with valid timing (for example iat={{now_epoch}}, exp={{now_epoch_plus_60}} or within configured max) alongside attack assertions to distinguish timing rejection from broken client configuration.

For I3 config-change sequences, Keycloak client policy and client configuration changes are intended to take effect on new requests. A valid coherence test must show that a new login after tightening config is rejected; it is BY DESIGN that behavior changes after admin updates. Do not flag mere post-update rejection as a bug.

For I5 audience tests, Keycloak does not automatically add the frontend client itself to the access token audience. Audience is added via Audience Resolve or hardcoded Audience mappers/client scopes. Therefore, empty or missing aud is often a configuration outcome, not a validation bypass. The fuzzer MUST explicitly configure audience mappers/client scopes before testing audience_mismatch or empty_audience.

For I5 token exchange tests, Keycloak documents a downscope-assertion-grant-enforcer client policy executor that restricts exchanged scopes to those already present in the subject_token, except default scopes with Include in token scope=false. The fuzzer MUST know whether this executor is enabled. Without it, expanded scopes may be by configuration; with it, extra requested scopes should be rejected.

Role mappings in tokens are the intersection of roles assigned to the user and role scope mappings/client scopes permitted to the client. For I5 authorization-binding tests, the fuzzer MUST treat missing roles as expected unless both the user assignment and client scope mapping sides are configured. Do not interpret absent roles as evidence of over-restriction bugs.

Client secret rotation is not automatic. Rotation occurs only on client update, regenerate secret, or explicit Admin REST force rotation. Rotated Secret Expiration has sentinel semantics: value 0 means the old secret is removed immediately during rotation. For I3 secret-rotation tests, the fuzzer MUST trigger an update/regeneration event and MUST account for 0 meaning no overlap window for the old secret.
Rotated Secret Expiration must always be smaller than Secret Expiration. For setup, the fuzzer MUST respect this invariant or client policy configuration is invalid.

PKCE method has sentinel semantics: blank means PKCE is not required, though PKCE is still accepted if the client sends PKCE parameters; 'S256' requires S256; 'plain' requires plain. For I3 pkce_skip and pkce_not_required_public_client tests, the fuzzer MUST explicitly set pkce_code_challenge_method to S256 or plain when testing enforcement. Leaving it blank does not disable PKCE support; it disables the requirement only.
oidc_jwt.source: Basic configuration / PKCE method

oidc_jwt.constraint: For OIDC step-up and ACR tests, Default ACR Values do not reliably enforce a level because the client can send acr_values=1 or other lower values and Keycloak will use them. To enforce a minimum authentication level, the fuzzer MUST configure Minimum ACR Value rather than relying on default ACR values.
oidc_jwt.source: Advanced configuration / ACR to Level of Authentication Mapping

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I3 config-change sequences involving ACR/LoA, changing client or realm configuration affects NEW logins by design. A valid coherence test must compare behavior of the same request before and after the config change, not treat the admin change itself as a bug.
oidc_jwt.source: Authentication flows / step-up and client ACR configuration

oidc_jwt.constraint: When testing I1 or I3 around request parameters such as claims or acr_values, these parameters can be modified by the user in the browser URL. The documentation states clients should mitigate this with PAR or a signed request object. Therefore, the fuzzer MUST use a signed request object when testing integrity of authorization request parameters; otherwise parameter tampering may be possible by design and is not a Keycloak verification failure.
oidc_jwt.source: Authentication flows / step-up mechanism warning

oidc_jwt.constraint: For OIDC request object signature tests (oidc_request_object_alg_none), client policies can enforce request object security, but absent such policy/client configuration the platform may accept weaker behavior by configuration. The fuzzer MUST first configure a client policy/profile that enforces request object signing requirements before treating acceptance of an unsigned or weakly signed request object as an I1 violation.
oidc_jwt.source: Client Policies / executors enforce OIDC request object satisfying high security level

oidc_jwt.constraint: Token exchange and JWT authorization grant scope restriction is only enforced when the downscope-assertion-grant-enforcer client policy executor is applied. Without this executor, requesting broader scope during token exchange may reflect configuration rather than a vulnerability. For I5 token_exchange_scope_escalation tests, the fuzzer MUST enable this executor on the target client before asserting that extra scopes should be rejected.
oidc_jwt.source: Client Policies / executors and Client Scopes / Downscoping

oidc_jwt.constraint: The downscope-assertion-grant-enforcer allows only downscoping relative to the presented subject_token/assertion. Default scopes with 'Include in token scope' set to false are an exception and may still appear because they are considered compulsory and invisible to the requester. For I5 scope-escalation tests, the fuzzer MUST NOT flag such invisible default scopes as escalation.
oidc_jwt.source: Client Scopes / Downscoping

oidc_jwt.constraint: Audience in access tokens is not automatically the frontend client itself. By design, the frontend client is not automatically added to the access token aud claim. For I5 audience tests, the fuzzer MUST explicitly configure audience via Audience or Audience Resolve mappers/client scopes; otherwise missing audience is expected behavior, not a validation bug.
oidc_jwt.source: Audience support / note on frontend client not automatically added

oidc_jwt.constraint: Audience Resolve adds a client as audience only when the current token has at least one client role for that client. If the user lacks such client role, the audience will not be included. For I5 audience_mismatch and empty_audience tests, the fuzzer MUST ensure the user has the relevant client role and that the client scope carrying that role is requested or linked as default; otherwise missing aud is expected setup behavior.
oidc_jwt.source: Audience support / Automatically add audience based on client roles

oidc_jwt.constraint: Optional client scopes are applied only when requested by the scope parameter in the authorization request. Default client scopes are always applied. For I5 tests that depend on claims, roles, or audiences from optional scopes, the fuzzer MUST include the exact scope value in start_oidc_auth or token requests; otherwise the claim omission is by design.
oidc_jwt.source: Client scopes / Link client scope with the client

oidc_jwt.constraint: Client scope permissioning is intersection-based: if a client scope has role scope mappings, the user must be a member of at least one mapped role or the scope's protocol mappers and role mappings are not applied, and the scope will not appear in the token. For I5 tests, the fuzzer MUST ensure the test user is permitted to use the client scope; otherwise missing claims or roles are expected.
oidc_jwt.source: Client scopes permissions

oidc_jwt.constraint: Exact matching semantics apply to Valid Redirect URIs except for the documented trailing wildcard behavior. Redirect URI comparison is case sensitive. For multi-identity or multi-client tests, the fuzzer MUST register each concrete redirect URI variant it intends to use; do not assume wildcard or case-insensitive matching.
oidc_jwt.source: Basic configuration / Valid Redirect URIs

oidc_jwt.constraint: Client secret rotation does not happen automatically in the background. Rotation occurs only on client update, regenerate secret, dynamic client update within the configured window, or explicit force rotation via Admin REST API. For I3 jwt_signing_key_rotation or secret-rotation coherence tests, the fuzzer MUST trigger an update/regenerate action after changing policy; merely waiting will not rotate the secret.
oidc_jwt.source: Client Secret Rotation

oidc_jwt.constraint: Rotated Secret Expiration must always be smaller than Secret Expiration. The fuzzer MUST respect this ordering when configuring secret rotation policies or setup will be invalid.
oidc_jwt.source: Creating an OIDC Client Secret Rotation Policy

oidc_jwt.constraint: For JWT client authentication ('Signed JWT' and 'Signed JWT with Client Secret'), Max expiration defaults to 60 seconds and tokens received after this period are rejected as too old. For I2 freshness tests, the fuzzer SHOULD use iat={{now_epoch}} and exp={{now_epoch_plus_60}} or shorter for control assertions, and use older assertions to test rejection. Do not assume long-lived client assertions are valid.
oidc_jwt.source: Confidential client credentials / Signed JWT

oidc_jwt.constraint: Replay of the same JWT bearer token is generally by design for stateless JWT validation. The documentation only describes expiration checks for JWT client assertions and does not describe jti replay tracking. For I2 replay_same_token and stateless_jwt_no_jti, the fuzzer MUST treat replay detection as a hardening check, not a vulnerability, unless testing client assertions with explicit one-time semantics configured elsewhere.
oidc_jwt.source: JWT/OIDC docs and RFC-aligned behavior in docs

oidc_jwt.constraint: Authentication sessions usually expire after 30 minutes by default, controlled by Login timeout. In multi-tab/browser authorization flows, expired authentication sessions can cause protocol-specific errors and automatic retries. For I3 flow-coherence tests, the fuzzer MUST keep authorization-code sequences within the login timeout and avoid interpreting expired-auth-session errors as state-swap or code-injection vulnerabilities.
oidc_jwt.source: Authentication sessions

oidc_jwt.constraint: User session limits use numeric sentinel 0 to disable the check for both realm session limit and client session limit. Value 0 does not mean zero sessions allowed. The fuzzer MUST treat 0 as 'disabled' when configuring session-limit-related tests.
oidc_jwt.source: User session limits

oidc_jwt.constraint: When user session limits are configured, the authenticator should be added to Browser, Direct Grant, Reset Credentials, and Post Broker Login flows, and for Browser it should not be placed at top level with Cookie because SSO re-authentication would be checked incorrectly. For I3 tests involving repeated logins or brokered logins, the fuzzer MUST account for flow placement; otherwise denials may be due to session-limit configuration rather than token or flow bugs.
oidc_jwt.source: User session limits

oidc_jwt.constraint: For token freshness tests against access tokens, client-level Access Token Lifespan overrides the realm setting. Client Session Idle/Max and offline session settings can also override realm defaults. The fuzzer MUST read or set client-specific timeout overrides before asserting expiration behavior.
oidc_jwt.source: Advanced Settings for OIDC

oidc_jwt.constraint: OAuth 2.0 Mutual TLS Certificate Bound Access Tokens and DPoP create holder-of-key tokens. UserInfo and token refresh requests with such tokens require proof of possession. For verify_granted_identity and other session-token calls, the fuzzer MUST NOT use bearer-style requests if the client is configured for MTLS-bound or DPoP-bound tokens, or failures will be by design.
oidc_jwt.source: Advanced configuration / MTLS bound tokens and DPoP

oidc_jwt.constraint: For token introspection, Keycloak can return JWT when Accept: application/jwt is used, especially useful for lightweight access tokens. If the fuzzer expects full claims from introspection of lightweight tokens, it SHOULD request the documented representation accordingly; otherwise claim absence in the access token itself may be by design.
oidc_jwt.source: Protocol mappers / Using lightweight access token

oidc_jwt.constraint: Lightweight access tokens intentionally omit PII and only include claims whose protocol mappers have 'Add to lightweight access token' enabled. Claims may still be available via introspection if 'Add to token introspection' is enabled. For I4/I5 tests comparing token contents, the fuzzer MUST distinguish lightweight-token omission from authorization failure.
oidc_jwt.source: Protocol mappers / Using lightweight access token
